title: Hardware mapping
heading: Keep every connection organised.
intro: Give switches, coils and lights clear names, assign their functions and configure supported drivers from one hardware view.
points: Name your connections
Give connections meaningful names that are easier to recognise throughout your project.
Set functions and drivers
Choose pin functions and applicable drivers from one hardware view.
seo_description: Give switches, coils and lights meaningful names. Configure GPIO functions and output drivers together in a visual homebrew pinball hardware map.

title: ESP connection
heading: See your controller connection.
intro: Check the connection between the Raspberry Pi and ESP32-S3, view controller details and access bridge controls in one place.
points: Check connection and firmware
Check device identity, connection status and firmware information in one place.
Manage the bridge
Manage the bridge and access controller utilities without leaving the application.
seo_title: Raspberry Pi to ESP32 Pinball Connection
seo_description: Connect your Raspberry Pi pinball host to an ESP32 controller. Check bridge status, controller identity and firmware from the ESPLink interface.

title: Firmware
heading: Manage ESP firmware versions.
intro: See available firmware releases and prepare the version you want to use with your connected controller.
points: Review available versions
See available versions and release information before preparing an update.
Prepare firmware for ESPLink
Download firmware for use with the connected ESP through ESPLink.

title: Accelerometer
heading: Monitor table movement.
intro: With a supported motion sensor connected, check table level and see nudge, lift and orientation readings in the browser.
points: Set a level reference
Save a level reference that reflects how your sensor is mounted.
See motion readings
View pitch, roll and sensor activity when a supported accelerometer is connected.

title: Supported components
heading: Check hardware compatibility before you build.
intro: Review components and platforms used with Pinball CTL, including which have been verified and which still need testing.
points: See verified hardware
Use the support guide to see what has been used and verified in the project.
Understand support limits
Supported, limited and untested components are distinguished so you can plan your own testing.

title: Rule editor
heading: Decide what happens in your game.
intro: Create rules that connect machine events to conditions and actions, and review the logic in one visual editor.
points: Connect events and actions
Define what should happen when an input or game event occurs.
Review your rules
Review your rules in one place as the machine evolves.

title: Scoring & combinations
heading: Make every shot count.
intro: Give targets, combinations and game moments their reward with scoring rules authored alongside the rest of your machine.
points: Reward the right moments
Connect events to scoring behaviour that suits your game.
Build combinations
Use combinations and multipliers to give players reasons to try the next shot.

title: Playfield layout
heading: Put your ideas on the playfield.
intro: Create a visual model of your machine and give its components a place, appearance and input mapping.
points: Arrange your machine
Position and customise components in the visual editor.
Make testing tangible
Bind keys and explore component responses while developing your layout.

title: Audio cues & outputs
heading: Give every moment its sound.
intro: Organise sound assets, create playback cues and route audio to the outputs that make sense for your cabinet.
points: Build your sound library
Upload, name and preview audio from one workspace.
Shape playback
Configure cues and output routing so sound becomes part of the game experience.

title: Media & displays
heading: Create a world beyond the playfield.
intro: Compose scenes from text, images, video and Godot content, then choose where they appear on your machine.
points: Compose your scenes
Bring visual layers and custom fonts together in the Media workspace.
Make displays work together
Choose scene destinations and startup content for configured displays.

title: Godot integration
heading: Bring your own interactive scenes.
intro: Use Godot to create animated backglass scenes, menus and custom score displays that become part of your Pinball CTL project.
points: Create in a familiar editor

Build and test your content in Godot, then import its exported scene pack. The bundled backglass includes a seven-shot cinematic attract sequence, a quest menu, a fast spinning bonus tally, animated award bursts and a preview theatre for testing without cabinet hardware. All 25 screens can be installed as individual Media scenes with flipper and Select navigation.
Connect scenes to gameplay
Map machine inputs to scene interactions and use supported events to connect back to rules.
seo_title: Godot Backglass Integration for Homebrew Pinball
seo_description: Build backglass scenes in Godot and connect them to pinball game events. Bring custom displays into the pinballCTL media workflow.

title: Dashboard
heading: Know where your machine stands.
intro: Get an overview of connectivity, runtime services and controller state before you start building or testing.
points: Start with the essentials
Bring key status information together instead of checking each module separately.
Follow up with detail
Use the overview to decide where to investigate next.
seo_description: Check bridge health, ESP32 status and performance from your pinball machine dashboard. Open detailed diagnostics directly from the overview.

title: Event logs
heading: Follow what happened.
intro: Explore runtime messages and event streams from your browser to understand how your machine responds.
points: Choose your perspective
Switch between web, bridge, ESP and event logs.
Find the signal
Filter the visible log output to focus your investigation.

title: Service log
heading: Give your machine a memory.
intro: Keep a record of physical maintenance and repairs, so the next adjustment starts with the history of the last one.
points: Record the work
Capture service and repair entries as your machine changes.
Find past fixes
Filter maintenance records by service type and date.

title: Integrity check
heading: Catch loose ends in your configuration.
intro: Check references across your project to spot broken links and unused items as rules, hardware and creative assets change.
points: See the connections
Audit dependencies across hardware, rules, layout, lighting, audio and scoring.
Review before resolving
Inspect reported errors and unused items to guide your cleanup.

title: Settings
heading: Make the project your own.
intro: Manage installation preferences and project data from one place, from your project name to import and export.
points: Set up your workspace
Configure project identity and installation-wide preferences.
Take your project with you
Use import and export tools to manage project data transfers.

title: Wi-Fi
heading: Keep your cabinet connected.
intro: View the host network state and manage Wi-Fi settings through the web interface on supported platforms.
points: Check the connection
See network name, IP address and connection status.
Update from the browser
Set network credentials through the Wi-Fi module where platform support is available.

title: Performance
heading: See how your game keeps up.
intro: Follow event throughput, delivery latency and queued work in one live view. Understand busy moments and find where your machine needs attention.
points: Watch the whole event path
Compare incoming events, host processing and ESP confirmations with one- and five-minute charts.
Find delays before they build
See queued work, the oldest waiting event and delivery latency together, so a busy machine is easier to diagnose.
Understand protective stops
View overload status and recovery behaviour without changing the firmware’s coil safety limits.
seo_description: Track event rates, queue depth and ESP32 delivery latency over time. Diagnose delays and understand protective overload handling in pinballCTL.
